newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 31.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- Fifteen people were killed in a double suicide bombing in Jerusalem's main Jewish market on Wednesday in an attack that put the brakes on a U.S. effort to revive peace talks between Israel and the Palestinians.

- The Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) has decided to soften its previous uncompromising position on the Basic Conditions of Employment Bill, opening the way for a resumption of talks with government and business.
- Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals said on Wednesday he hoped that monetary policy could be relaxed before the end of the year.
- Gauteng Housing Minister Dan Mofokeng was acquitted in the Germiston Regional Court on Wednesday on three charges of contravening the Arms and Ammunition Act.
- Cellular telephone supplier Radiospoor has been pressured into dropping a newspaper advertisement addressing President Nelson Mandela on crime after a complaint from a government official.
BUSINESS REPORT

- Engen Ltd shares have lost 12.50 rand, or 36 percent of their value, in the 13 months since Petronas, the Malaysian oil company, acquired a 30 percent stake for 34,50 rand a share last June. The share closed at 22 rand on Wednesday.
- Cosatu said it would go ahead with three weeks of nationwide rolling mass action during August, starting on Monday, to press for its key demands on the draft Basic Conditions of Employment Bill.
- DataTec, the JSE-listed networking technology and services group, has bought Logical Networks, a British networking company, for $25 million.
- The rand had been one of the weakest currencies in the South African Development Community (SADC) over the past 18 months, Investec Securities said recently.
SAKE BEELD

- The country's largest trade union federation Cosatu said it would go ahead with a planned strike on Monday over the planned employment bill, but sources indicated the federation would seek to negotiate outstanding issues rather than risk the bill being withdrawn.
- South Africa's financial markets reacted positively to Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals' comments that an interest rate cut was still possible before the end of the year.

- South African gold mines played their part in the three months to end-June to keep the industry afloat, restricting production costs and keeping gold production relatively constant despite the disruption of several public holidays.
THE STAR
- World leaders reacted with horror to an attack on Wednesday by two suicide bombers in Israel, fearing the 14 deaths and 157 injuries could destroy hopes of Middle East peace.

- The African National Congress' transport department employs some of Johannesburg's most errant drivers, with at least 24 outstanding warrants of arrest for the contravention of various fines amounting to more than 6,000 rand.
